config.title: Request Deduplication

intro.title: Request Deduplication
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that fetches user data from a mock API. You'll learn how to implement request deduplication, a technique that prevents sending multiple identical API requests at the same time. This concept uses a caching mechanism to store ongoing requests, ensuring only one request is made for duplicate calls. You'll work with React hooks like useState and useEffect, and use TypeScript to define types for your data and functions. By the end, you'll understand how deduplication improves performance and reduces unnecessary network traffic in your applications.
intro.usecase: Request deduplication is essential in modern web applications where multiple UI components might trigger the same API call simultaneously. In dashboard interfaces, multiple widgets displaying related metrics could independently request the same user data, causing unnecessary network traffic. Search autocomplete components benefit from deduplication when rapid keystrokes trigger identical queries, preventing redundant API calls. E-commerce product filters that update multiple display areas simultaneously also rely on this pattern to avoid duplicate inventory checks and ensure consistent data across the interface.

objectives: Implement a deduplication cache to store ongoing requests
Construct a custom hook that manages request deduplication logic
Apply deduplication to prevent duplicate API calls for identical requests
Configure TypeScript interfaces for deduplication cache entries
Initialize request tracking with unique identifiers
Integrate deduplication logic with existing API fetching patterns
Manipulate cache state to clear completed requests

steps.title: Initialize state for request tracking
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use useState to create a state variable named 'pendingRequests' with proper TypeScript type annotation to track in-flight requests. Initialize it as an empty array.
steps.hint: Use useState<RequestType[]> to specify the type. Since we're tracking request IDs, you can use string[] as the type for now.

steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an async fetchData function that returns a promise resolving with mock data after a delay, ready to be used for request deduplication.
successCriteria: The App component contains an async fetchData function that returns a promise resolving with a string after 2 seconds.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function is async, returns a promise, and resolves with mock data after a 2-second delay.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetchData function needs to be async and simulate a network request with a delay. Try creating a function that returns a promise with setTimeout.

steps.title: Implement request deduplication logic
steps.instruction: Modify the makeRequest function to check if a request with the same ID is already pending before calling fetchData. If it is pending, return the existing promise instead of starting a new request.
steps.hint: Before calling fetchData, check if the requestId already exists in pendingRequests. If it does, return early without making a new request.
steps.expectedOutcome: The makeRequest function now includes a check to prevent duplicate requests for the same requestId.
successCriteria: The makeRequest function checks pendingRequests before calling fetchData and returns early if the requestId already exists.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
